subject: [RFC PATCH 0/5] mm/page_alloc: keep non-movable pages out of movable pageblocks for THP

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary: Reviewer Dev Jain noted that the patch series as-is would regress performance by allowing unmovable pageblocks to contain movable allocations, which could prevent mTHP allocation rescues.
reviews.raw_body:
I think your patch series applied as-is would regress stuff:
we may have lots of UNMOVABLE pageblocks with lots of
movable allocations, unable to be rescued, hurting mTHP
allocations.

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author is seeking feedback on how to proceed with the patch series, asking if reviewers want to review it in stages or post a larger series all at once.
reviews.raw_body:
How should we move forward with this?

Do do guys want to review this series first,
and then I post an update with the other
stuff, before any gets merged?

Or do you want me to post a larger series
all at once?

Before I move on, do the combined policy
changes from patches 3, 4, and 5 make sense
to you (with or without evacuation) ?

Patch 1 from this series can be merged all
by itself as a separate thing.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-10-15.patch_summary: This patch series addresses issues with Transparent Huge Pages (THP) allocation by keeping non-movable pages out of movable pageblocks. The current page allocation policies cause THP allocation success rates to drop under sustained non-movable demand. The patches modify the pageblock claiming and stealing policies, ensuring that non-movable pages are not mixed with movable-type page blocks. This is done by converting movable blocks for non-movable allocations when necessary, skipping movable blocks on non-movable steals, and claiming movable blocks fully taken by non-movable compaction capture. The goal is to prevent polluting movable blocks with non-movable content and concentrate kernel allocations in fewer pageblocks.
